subject: BrightLane private GPU pool: throughput goals & staged scaling proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Holt <jordan.holt@brightlane.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: 2026-10-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightLane private GPU pool — initial throughput targets?

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. We ran a quick internal check and wanted to capture the ask concretely so your team can recommend a sizing plan. Fleeting summary:
- Primary workload: real-time summarization + reranking for clinical note ingestion (p50 latency target ~200ms per request, p95 <600ms)
- Expected steady QPS (user-facing): 120 requests/sec during peak windows (3x spikes anticipated around 10am/2pm/8pm)
- Payload profile: average prompt length ~520 tokens, response ~240 tokens; occasional long context up to 2k tokens but rare (~2% of traffic)
- Data residency: must run in our VPC in us-east-1; encryption at rest and KMS managed

Can you share a recommended baseline throughput target (tokens/sec or GPUs) and a staged scaling plan (warm pools / burst / failover) for a Private deployment? Also attaching our workload summary CSV in case that's helpful.

Appreciate any high-level numbers you can share — Jordan

Attachments: brightlane_workload_summary.csv (csv)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
To: Jordan Holt <jordan.holt@brightlane.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
Date: 2026-10-27T12:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane private GPU pool — initial throughput targets?

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear profile and the CSV. Quick read-through below and a proposed starting point — see the attached spreadsheet for the worked math. High level recommendation: staged capacity based on sustained token throughput with a small warm burst pool.

Summary proposal (baseline):
- Target sustained throughput: ~1.2M tokens/sec aggregate (accounts for p50/p95 shapes and average prompt+response)
- Equivalent starting fleet: 8 A100-40GB equiv GPUs running quantized fp16 model variant with continuous batching and prefix cache enabled; this gives ~150k tokens/sec per GPU sustained (estimate depends on kernel set)
- Warm burst pool: reserve 2 GPUs warm (idle KV cached) to absorb short spikes (x1.5-factoring for 30s windows)
- Long tail spikes: allow autoscale + reserved burst to scale to 12 GPUs for sustained surges >5min
- Headroom policy: maintain 15–20% headroom on baseline during business hours to preserve p95 SLOs when cache miss and jitter occur

Networking notes:
- Egress: set egress budget to accommodate token output (estimate ~0.6KB per response on average); coordinate with your infra to ensure NAT/gateway throughput >1Gbps per 4 GPUs to avoid bottlenecks
- Latency: colocate model servers in a single AZ where possible to minimize cross-AZ hops; use intra-VPC ENIs with enhanced networking

Open questions from our side (to size more precisely):
1) What fraction of requests require the long-context path (>1k tokens)? you noted ~2% — confirm if that’s per peak or overall
2) Are you ok running a small quantized variant for production? we can recommend fallback to full-precision for quality-sensitive calls
3) Any existing NIC-level bandwidth constraints or gateway egress limits we should assume?

Attachments: k_i_throughput_proposal_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

If useful we can schedule a 30-min sizing call with our infra team and a quick network readout. I can also produce a conservative and an aggressive sizing column in the sheet.

—Karthik

Looping in the ops sizing perspective — following up on Karthik's estimate.

Quick ops notes and a couple of conservative adjustments:
- We should add a separate hot-KV cache tier per AZ for the 2% long context traffic if those requests are latency sensitive; moving the KV cache to a dedicated host reduces eviction-related latency spikes
- For network egress: recommend NIC bonding (2 x 25Gb) per GPU host if BrightLane wants to sustain the high burst windows without NAT throttling; point-of-fact: many on-prem racks default to 10Gb which will be a chokepoint here
- Autoscale cadence: prefer step autoscaling (add 1–2 GPUs per minute) with admission control to avoid jitter-induced thundering; don't allow instantaneous scale >25% of current fleet

Operational checklist item we recommend BrightLane confirm: firewall rules enabling internal pod-to-pod comms, MTU settings (9000 recommended for large payloads), and any outbound proxy that might rewrite TLS causing performance issues.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Appreciate the follow-ups. We've put together a short mutual action plan and a draft SOW to unblock procurement — links below. Answers inline:

NIC recommendation: 10Gb is a likely bottleneck for the sustained/peak math above. We recommend 25Gb NICs per host as the baseline for any host running 1–2 GPUs; for 4+ GPUs per host consider 50Gb. The rule of thumb we used: provision ~1Gbps per 100k tokens/sec outbound, plus buffer for TLS overhead and multiplexing.

p95 with 2.5% long-context: with the recommended warm-KV cache and headroom policy (15–20%), yes — p95 remains <600ms for the majority of requests. The long-context path will still pull p95 upward; we propose routing long-context requests to a separate lane with slightly relaxed p95 (target 900ms) or to a fallback full-precision model to protect the main SLO.

Attachments and links:
- Draft SOW (SOW_BrightLane_draft.docx) — includes milestones: network readiness, initial 8-GPU provisioning, 2-week soak, and staged scale to 12 GPUs
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cBRIGHTLANE (contains the sizing workbook and network diagram)
- DocuSign placeholder: DocuSign: 0a1b2c3d-BrightLane-SOW

Next steps we propose:
- Karthik/Laura/Stef to run a 45-min technical sizing call with BrightLane infra + procurement next Tue (suggest 10am ET)
- We will produce a conservative (cost-optimized) and aggressive (low-latency) column in the sizing workbook by EOD Monday
- Procurement: we will add a simple monthly egress estimate in the SOW draft (ballpark) by Monday

If that works I'll send a calendar invite and attach the draft SOW for your internal review.

Thanks — Karthik
